newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada 1997 all wheat seeding intentions fall.
newsitem.headline: Canada 1997 all wheat seeding intentions fall.

text.p: Statistics Canada on Wednesday released the following 1996 planting intention forecasts based on a survey done in the last week of March, before the flooding in Manitoba (millions of acres, percentage changes):

Statistics Canada said farmers plan to switch about three million acres, mostly from wheat, into canola this year. Producers appear to be motivated by steady international demand and predicted higher prices for canola, the federal agency said.

The agency said weakened world prices for wheat partially explain farmers' intentions to plant 2.9 million fewer acres of spring wheat in the 1997-98 crop year. This loss is spread across the Prairie provinces, which together plant over 95 percent of the spring wheat area.

As for canola, Canada's major oilseed, the Prairie provinces are reported to be seeding 2.8 million more acres of canola. Total acreage for Canada will not approach the record set in 1994 at 14.3 million acres, but it does reverse the downward trend since that time.
Other planting intentions included (millions of acres, percentage changes) :

Statistics Canada officials said flooding in Manitoba has affected less than four percent of the cultivated land in that province, but they will not know the full effect of the flooding for about three or four weeks.
